cases.title: An AP repertoire with ordinary resources
cases.subject: compositions
cases.original_question: What two or three AP comps are worth learning on 18.3B without relying on an artifact, emblem, or a big reroll high roll, and what core units and item needs distinguish them?
cases.question: What two or three AP comps are worth learning on 18.3B without relying on an artifact, emblem, or a big reroll high roll, and what core units and item needs distinguish them?
cases.scenario: An AP learning repertoire for a verified 18.3B scope. Start with ordinary-item named carry builds and avoid relying on multiple three-star supports; Ahri/Soraka/Zyra are discovery leads rather than a closed eligible pool.
cases.plan: Use rank_units and rank_unit_loadouts to identify reportable AP-oriented candidates from context, then cohort unit/trait discovery and conjunction checks to define recurring support packages. Compare reportable named build/star/level cohorts and inspect global equipment distributions with query_cohort. State the candidate-pool coverage and what no-high-roll proxy was actually checked.
cases.checks: Provide two or three substantively different supported packages with core, item-holder needs, counts and mean/top4/win. Popularity alone is insufficient. Do not select only winning boards or equate final three-stars with luck. Missing eligible candidates/pages limits completeness.
cases.limits: No composition-cluster tool, generic AP filter, boardwide artifact/emblem exclusion or global three-star-count filter is exposed. A strictly ordinary whole-board/no-multiple-three-star benchmark needs a prepared population; current-tool results must be labeled ordinary carry builds with inspected support, not falsely certified full-resource eligibility.

cases.title: Does Veigar belong in a top-four repertoire?
cases.subject: compositions
cases.original_question: For an ordinary-item AP repertoire on 18.3B, should Veigar–Ornn be on my list if I care more about top fours than firsts, or is its good placement mostly coming from specialist-item boards?
cases.question: For an ordinary-item AP repertoire on 18.3B, should Veigar–Ornn be on my list if I care more about top fours than firsts, or is its good placement mostly coming from specialist-item boards?
cases.scenario: Veigar–Ornn ordinary versus specialist-item versions, with Veigar reroll permitted and top-four priority; compare a separately defined ordinary Zyra–Amumu package as repertoire context.
cases.plan: Discover Veigar loadouts and named Ornn/carry support cells, partition explicit holder trios and named special-item conditions, and compare within shared level/star/core strata. Use returned comparison histograms to count top-four outcomes for disjoint reportable categories; compare Zyra–Amumu as a separate package, not a matched Veigar swap.
cases.checks: Report both group top4_rate and contribution to the family's observed top fours, with the same denominator and nonoverlapping category definition. Include win-rate tradeoff and sample sizes. A higher artifact-group rate does not mean it supplies most successes.
cases.limits: Ordinary items on Veigar do not imply ordinary items across the board. Generic special-item-count predicates are absent, so whole-board partition/share claims need preparation or must remain explicitly incomplete. Do not sum overlapping special cohorts or multiply rounded rates into exact counts.

cases.title: What Azir-three statistics actually describe
cases.subject: compositions
cases.original_question: Is Azir reroll actually a reasonable comp to choose on 18.3B, or do his good three-star stats mostly come from boards where someone else is carrying? What would make the Azir version worth choosing?
cases.question: Is Azir reroll actually a reasonable comp to choose on 18.3B, or do his good three-star stats mostly come from boards where someone else is carrying? What would make the Azir version worth choosing?
cases.scenario: Azir3 end states partitioned by his completed-item investment and named teammate investment: primary-carry proxy, co-carry proxy, support proxy and ambiguous. Include a three-item Azir/zero-item Kha'Zix sensitivity.
cases.plan: Use query_cohort for joint named-unit star/item-count cells and repeated unit/trait discovery to identify recurring cores. Compare explicit role-proxy cohorts with shared level and named tank/carry conditions. Require Kha'Zix presence with zero items for that sensitivity, not absence mistaken for zero items.
cases.checks: Report role-cell counts/shares and placement/top4/win, preserving incomplete/ambiguous categories and actual denominator coverage. Distinguish high-performing itemized Azir end states from the probability that choosing reroll succeeds.
cases.limits: No actual damage role, attempt-level reroll denominator, generic teammate investment sum, form or sacrifice choice. The whole role partition may be incomplete under bounded candidate enumeration; label it rather than forcing every board into a role.
